items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: I was playing at the Mantis in 1917. James P. Europe from New York came then with his band... So he asked me, he says, bro, come on down to me. I'm going to hear the 15th band. I said, you might enjoy that. So I said, yeah, okay. So we went on down.

ctx.x: I was playing at the Mantis in 1917. James P. Europe from New York came then with his band, the 15th. That was one of the, at that time, they were one of the finest military bands I ever heard. And he had 12 clarinet players. So he came in the ducks and he listened to Sidney. So he called Sidney over to the table, him and Noble Sisson of New York. And he asked Sidney to join his band. Would he join his band? Can Sidney join his band? He said, well, Mr. Europe, he said, I don't read. He said, I'd like for you to…
Did Ellington write much of that out at all? So when we say like black and tan fantasy, when you make that up?
